problem_type: paid generation reference upload scope invalidation
symptom: After a real delayed reference-image upload, clicking the spend confirmation is refused with generation_reference_scope_changed; no request is created, the card remains unchanged, and the user sees no reason.
direct_cause: appIntegration and mcpStdioServer each compare the whole project revision and Run revision after resolveProductionReferenceUrls returns. The real upload window can contain Nomi-owned project/cache/canvas writes, so the duplicated assertCurrent rejects its own writes.
class_root: The upload-time guard has no shared semantic snapshot that separates user-visible generation scope (project identity, selected candidate/reference identities, and the selected shot's Run state) from Nomi-owned projection/cache revisions.
affected_population: Agent-panel and authenticated MCP reference-image generations
Any provider whose real asset localization is asynchronous
macOS and other platforms where canvas/cache writes overlap the upload window
internal_only_reason: This is an application-owned authorization invariant; provider upload behavior is already covered by the existing asset-localization contract and does not decide the scope rule.
invariants: Nomi-owned project/cache/canvas projection writes during reference localization do not invalidate a still-current user-approved generation scope.
A changed project binding, selected candidate/reference identity/content, or selected shot Run semantic state fails closed before an authorization envelope is returned.
Both production hosts call the same shared scope guard and expose the structured refusal through the existing spend-card i18n path.

door_reduction.why_not: The two host entry doors remain for app Agent and authenticated MCP, while a single shared read guard replaces their duplicated local assertions; the extra listed door is the centralized owner, not a new rule.

generality_proof: The guard snapshots the semantic candidate/reference and selected-shot Run state before any resolver, then re-reads the same fields after every asynchronous resolver callback. It intentionally ignores project and Run revision counters and canvas binding/cache fields, so every provider, caller, and platform using the shared authorization helper gets the same behavior while user edits or external Run progress still fail closed.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Capture and assert the stable project binding, selected candidate/reference identities, and selected-shot Run semantic state while excluding Nomi-owned projection/cache revisions.
Keep the structured approval-stale refusal on the existing bilingual visible toast.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: App Agent panel calls prepareProductionGenerationAuthorizationWithReferences and will receive the shared guard through its assertCurrent callback. The new agentPanelSpendReferences.e2e.test.ts and agent-reference-upload-scope.walk.mjs exercise this host with a real held multipart upload.
The stdio host calls the same shared authorization helper and no longer owns a second comparison.
Its existing failed() path carries approval_stale to the renderer; only the source guard changes.

recurrence.reason: Any asynchronous provider upload, cache write, canvas projection, platform file watcher, or alternate host can advance revision counters during the same confirmation window.
same_class_scan: rg generation_reference_scope_changed electron src tests scripts
Checked appIntegration and mcpStdioServer as independent production hosts; both duplicated the same assertion before this fix.

prevention.invariant: Only user-meaningful generation-scope fields may invalidate an authorization while reference localization is in flight; Nomi-owned projection/cache revision changes are ignored.
prevention.failure_mode: Throw generation_reference_scope_changed before an authorization envelope or provider submission is created.
prevention.strategy: Delete both host-local comparisons and make the shared authorization helper require the same guard callback for every asynchronous reference resolver.

legacy_paths.rationale: The duplicate host assertions and the test-only immediate URL bypass are obsolete paths that allowed the class to escape shared coverage.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The invariant is owned by Nomi authorization and asset-localization code; no third-party runtime controls scope comparison.

migration: No persisted schema changes. Existing pending cards and Runs keep their current shape; the next confirmation captures the new semantic scope and either proceeds or returns the existing failed card with approval_stale.
residual_risks: The true paid provider run remains unverified until coordination executes the paid sample on the merged build.
A provider-specific upload adapter outside resolveProductionReferenceUrls is not covered unless it enters the shared authorization helper; door-map and tests cover the two current production hosts.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The shared guard owns the semantic snapshot and both hosts call it; the listed tests prove self-write tolerance and user-scope rejection.
